• No. Kegan’s 4242 branches do the opposite: prev_state_events is only interpreted after Synapse already has a RoomVersion.

  Examples in upstream/kegan/4242-inbound:

  - Existing-room reads call store.get_room_version(room_id) before parsing PDUs.
  - /make_join supplies the expected room_version; that version is passed into send_join.
  - For MSC4242, send_join reads state_dag, finds the create event inside it, and verifies create.content.room_version ==
    expected_room_version.

  - Only then does it use prev_state_events as State-DAG edges: fetching prior state, ordering persistence, calculating auth,
    and walking missing-event paths.

  So there is no “inspect prev_state_events, therefore this is v12/MSC4242” path. That would be circular and unsafe: you need
  the room-version rules to know whether prev_state_events is meaningful, required, canonicalized, and included in the event
  hash/signature.

  The relevant shape is effectively:

  existing room: room_id → rooms.room_version → parse event

  remote join:  /make_join.room_version → parse event/send_join
                                    ↓
                        create event confirms it
                                    ↓
                     interpret prev_state_events

  Nico is right about validation: even if an ID encoded a version hint, Synapse must still retrieve and validate the create
  event. A version hint could avoid a lookup only in a narrowly defined bootstrap path; it cannot replace create-event
  validation or establish trust in an arbitrary received PDU.

      use std::str::FromStr;
      
      use conduwuit::{
      	Err, Error, Result, err,
      	matrix::event::{gen_event_id, gen_event_id_canonical_json},
      };
      use itertools::Itertools;
      use ruma::{
      	CanonicalJsonObject, CanonicalJsonValue, EventId, OwnedEventId, OwnedRoomId, RoomId,
      	RoomVersionId,
      	api::error::{ErrorKind, IncompatibleRoomVersionErrorData},
      	room_version_rules::RoomVersionRules,
      };
      use serde_json::value::RawValue as RawJsonValue;
      
      type Parsed = (OwnedRoomId, OwnedEventId, CanonicalJsonObject);
      
      /// Extracts the expected room ID from the PDU. If the PDU claims its own room
      /// ID, that is returned. Since `m.room.create` in v12 and onward lacks this
      /// field over federation, it will be calculated if not provided, otherwise a
      /// validation error will be returned.
      fn extract_room_id(event_type: &str, pdu: &CanonicalJsonObject) -> Result<OwnedRoomId> {
      	if let Some(room_id) = pdu.get("room_id").and_then(CanonicalJsonValue::as_str) {
      		return RoomId::parse(room_id)
      			.map_err(|e| err!(Request(BadJson("Invalid room_id {room_id:?} in pdu: {e}"))));
      	}
      	// If there's no room ID, and this is not a create event, it is illegal.
      	let is_create = event_type == "m.room.create"
      		&& pdu
      			.get("state_key")
      			.and_then(|v| v.as_str())
      			.is_some_and(str::is_empty);
      	if !is_create {
      		return Err!(Request(BadJson("Missing room_id in pdu")));
      	}
      
      	// Room versions 11 and below require the room ID is present.
      	let room_version = RoomVersionId::from_str(
      		pdu.get("content")
      			.and_then(CanonicalJsonValue::as_object)
      			.ok_or_else(|| err!(Request(InvalidParam("Missing or invalid content in pdu"))))?
      			.get("room_version")
      			.and_then(CanonicalJsonValue::as_str)
      			.unwrap_or("1"), // Omitted room versions default to v1
      	)
      	.map_err(|e| err!(Request(BadJson("Invalid room_version in pdu: {e}"))))?;
      
      	let Some(room_version_rules) = room_version.rules() else {
      		return Err!(Request(BadJson("Unknown room version in pdu")));
      	};
      
      	if room_version_rules.event_format.require_room_create_room_id {
      		return Err!(Request(BadJson("Missing room_id in pdu")));
      	}
      
      	let event_id = gen_event_id(pdu, &room_version_rules)?;
      	Ok(RoomId::parse(event_id.as_str().replace('$', "!"))
      		.expect("constructed room ID has to be valid"))
      }
      
      /// Parses every entry in an array as an event ID, returning an error if any
      /// step fails.
      pub(super) fn expect_event_id_array(
      	value: &CanonicalJsonObject,
      	field: &str,
      ) -> Result<Vec<OwnedEventId>> {
      	value
      		.get(field)
      		.ok_or_else(|| err!(Request(BadJson("missing field `{field}` on PDU"))))?
      		.as_array()
      		.ok_or_else(|| err!(Request(BadJson("expected an array PDU field `{field}`"))))?
      		.iter()
      		.map(|v| {
      			v.as_str()
      				.ok_or_else(|| {
      					err!(Request(BadJson("expected an array of event IDs for `{field}`")))
      				})
      				.and_then(|s| {
      					EventId::parse(s)
      						.map_err(|e| err!(Request(BadJson("invalid event ID in `{field}`: {e}"))))
      				})
      		})
      		.try_collect()
      }
      
      impl super::Service {
      	/// Parses an incoming PDU JSON object, generating an event ID for it and
      	/// attempts to discover the associated room ID. Does not insert the event
      	/// ID into the returned object.
      	pub async fn parse_incoming_pdu(
      		&self,
      		pdu: &RawJsonValue,
      		room_version_rules: Option<&RoomVersionRules>,
      	) -> Result<Parsed> {
      		let value = serde_json::from_str::<CanonicalJsonObject>(pdu.get()).map_err(|e| {
      			err!(BadServerResponse(debug_warn!("Error parsing incoming event {e:?}")))
      		})?;
      		let event_type = value
      			.get("type")
      			.and_then(CanonicalJsonValue::as_str)
      			.ok_or_else(|| err!(Request(InvalidParam("Missing or invalid type in pdu"))))?;
      
      		let room_id = extract_room_id(event_type, &value)?;
      
      		let room_version_rules = match room_version_rules {
      			| Some(r) => r,
      			| None => {
      				let room_version = self
      					.services
      					.state
      					.get_room_version(&room_id)
      					.await
      					.map_err(|_| err!(Request(NotFound("no version associated with room ID"))))?;
      				if matches!(room_version, RoomVersionId::V1 | RoomVersionId::V2) {
      					return Err(Error::BadRequest(
      						ErrorKind::IncompatibleRoomVersion(
      							IncompatibleRoomVersionErrorData::new(room_version),
      						),
      						"Room version is too old.",
      					));
      				}
      				&room_version
      					.rules()
      					.expect("room version must be supported")
      			},
      		};
      
      		let (event_id, value) =
      			gen_event_id_canonical_json(pdu, room_version_rules).map_err(|e| {
      				err!(Request(InvalidParam("Could not convert event to canonical json: {e}")))
      			})?;
      		// NOTE: validation checks are now performed by `pdu_format_check_1`.
      		Ok((room_id, event_id, value))
      	}
      }

      	/// Returns the room's version.
      	#[tracing::instrument(skip(self), level = "debug")]
      	pub async fn get_room_version(&self, room_id: &RoomId) -> Result<RoomVersionId> {
      		self.services

      			.room_state_get_content(room_id, &StateEventType::RoomCreate, "")
      			.await
      			.map(|content: RoomCreateEventContent| content.room_version)
      			.map_err(|e| err!(Request(NotFound("No create event found: {e:?}"))))
      	}

      			.get(room_id)
      			.await
      			.deserialized()
      	}

      	/// hash or sign the PDU, meaning it can be mutated after.
      	pub async fn create_event(
      		&self,
      		partial_pdu: PartialPdu,
      		sender: &UserId,
      		room_id: Option<&RoomId>,
      		_mutex_lock: &RoomMutexGuard,
      	) -> Result<(PduEvent, RoomVersionRules)> {
      		let PartialPdu {
      			event_type,
      			content,
      			sticky,
      			unsigned,
      			state_key,
      			redacts,
      			timestamp,
      		} = partial_pdu;
      
      		trace!(
      			"Creating event of type {} in room {}",
      			event_type,
      			room_id.as_ref().map_or("None", |id| id.as_str())
      		);
      		let room_version = match room_id {
      			| Some(room_id) => {
      				trace!(%room_id, "Looking up existing room ID");
      				self.services
      					.state
      					.get_room_version(room_id)
      					.await
      					.or_else(|_| {
      						room_version_from_event(
      							room_id.to_owned(),
      							&event_type.clone(),
      							&content.clone(),
      						)
      					})?
      			},
      			| None => {
      				trace!("No room ID, assuming room creation");
      				room_version_from_event(
      					RoomId::new_v1(self.services.globals.server_name()),
      					&event_type.clone(),
      					&content.clone(),
      				)?
      			},
      		};
      
      		let Some(room_version_rules) = room_version.rules() else {
      			return Err!(Request(UnsupportedRoomVersion("Unsupported room version")));
      		};
      
      		let prev_events: Vec<OwnedEventId> = match room_id {
      			| Some(room_id) =>
      				self.services
      					.state
      					.get_forward_extremities(room_id)
      					.take(20)
      					.map(Into::into)
      					.collect()
      					.await,
      			| None => Vec::new(),
      		};

## Assistant

No `prev_state_events` logic exists in Continuwuity’s Rust sources, so there is no path that infers a room version from it.

For ordinary inbound PDUs, it does:

`room_id → current m.room.create state → content.room_version → RoomVersionRules → parse/hash PDU`

See [parse_incoming_pdu.rs](/run/media/shane/shane4tb-ent/repos/continuwuity/src/service/rooms/event_handler/parse_incoming_pdu.rs:105) and [state/mod.rs](/run/media/shane/shane4tb-ent/repos/continuwuity/src/service/rooms/state/mod.rs:383). Auth-chain and fetched events are explicitly parsed with rules already obtained from the create event.

The one bootstrap-like exception is a v12+ `m.room.create` PDU without `room_id`: it reads that create event’s own `content.room_version` to select event-ID rules and derive the room ID. See [parse_incoming_pdu.rs](/run/media/shane/shane4tb-ent/repos/continuwuity/src/service/rooms/event_handler/parse_incoming_pdu.rs:17). That is still create-content-driven, not structural-field or predecessor-state inference.

Local event creation has a similar fallback for a brand-new create event: use its `room_version`; otherwise, retrieve it from room state. [create.rs](/run/media/shane/shane4tb-ent/repos/continuwuity/src/service/rooms/timeline/create.rs:104)

## Assistant

Yes — `room_id_or_hash()` is exactly that kind of structural version inference.

For an `m.room.create` event it does:

```rust
if room_id exists:  // “v1–v11”
    use it
else:               // “v12+”
    derive room ID by replacing `$` with `!` in event ID
```

It exists twice, for `PduEvent` and `PduBuilder`, in [pdu.rs](/run/media/shane/shane4tb-ent/repos/continuwuity/src/core/matrix/pdu.rs:123) and [pdu.rs](/run/media/shane/shane4tb-ent/repos/continuwuity/src/core/matrix/pdu.rs:197). It is used broadly for authorization, federation endpoint room checks, client responses, visibility checks, etc.

A few adjacent examples:

- The trait comment itself says it should only be used for “a v12 create event,” but the implementation only looks at event type plus `room_id` presence: [event.rs](/run/media/shane/shane4tb-ent/repos/continuwuity/src/core/matrix/event.rs:173).
- The pusher has the same assumption: no `room_id` means “Only v12+ create events”: [pusher/mod.rs](/run/media/shane/shane4tb-ent/repos/continuwuity/src/service/pusher/mod.rs:305).
- Inbound parsing is better: for a room-ID-less create event it reads `content.room_version`, obtains its rules, then allows/rejects the missing field based on `require_room_create_room_id`: [parse_incoming_pdu.rs](/run/media/shane/shane4tb-ent/repos/continuwuity/src/service/rooms/event_handler/parse_incoming_pdu.rs:37).

So: no `prev_state_events` inference, but yes, `room_id_or_hash()` is a concrete structural invariant / “this looks like v12” mechanism. It is currently spec-valid, but bakes in the assumption that any future room version which omits `room_id` uses the same `$event_id → !room_id` derivation.
